Hi Dylan —

Thanks for taking this on. We only need materials suitable for SIG review (some items will get redacted later). Our timeline is tight — can you provide an initial packet by Friday 2027-04-30?

Helpful context: we run multiple regulated workloads and want to validate cross-tenant isolation, control-plane separation, and egress policing. If you have a preferred redaction checklist for shared diagrams, include that too.

Nina Park

—Dylan

Dylan — adding a couple of clarifying points for the packet. Please quote below when you send.

On Tue, Apr 26, 2027 at 11:04 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com> wrote:
> Nina —
> 
> Appreciate the clear ask. We can get an initial packet to you by EOD Friday. High-level plan:
> 
> - Attach a one-page "isolation playbook" that outlines behavioral guarantees (control plane separation, network zoning, tenant fencing).
> - Provide an annotated topology SVG showing Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC + optional on-prem) overlays, with clear callouts for control/data plane separation and egress chokepoints.
> - Include an egress_policy_matrix CSV that lists allowed outbound destinations, NAT/egress gateway behavior, and logging/alerting hooks.

My additions:
- Control plane: always runs in a logically separate management plane with mutual TLS between control plane nodes and customer-specific agents where applicable. For Private deployments we recommend dedicated subnets for control-plane endpoints and LB-level ACLs; note that HSM/KMS calls are proxied through a customer-managed VPC endpoint when requested.
- Data plane (inference): per-tenant compute pools (Dedicated = physical GPU pools reserved for tenant; Private = isolated VPC subnets with security groups and microsegmentation). We use flow-level telemetry and prefix-based KV caching — telemetry streams surface token-level anonymized usage to ops (no raw customer prompts).
- Egress: default deny, explicit egress whitelist per deployment, egress gateway terminates TLS for outbound allowlist destinations only, and all egress flows are logged to the audit pipeline with retention aligned to the customer's profile.

I'll attach a short CSV summarizing the typical egress categories and where logs are emitted (edge gateway, LB, host agent).

Attachment: egress_policy_matrix.csv (draft)

-Karthik

Nina —

Attached is the initial SIG packet for Nimbus. Files are redacted to remove internal hostnames and non-essential telemetry endpoints. Summary below; full files attached and a read-only Drive folder is linked at the bottom.

Summary of artifacts provided:
- redwood_dedicated_private_isolation_v2.pdf — one-page isolation playbook with boundary guarantees, control/data plane separation notes, and recommended customer-side network controls for Private deployments.
- network_traffic_flows.svg — annotated topology showing: public control-plane endpoints (regionally routed), dedicated GPU pools per tenant (Reserved), and Private deployment VPC overlays. Callouts explain microsegmentation primitives and KV/prefix cache placement.
- egress_policy_matrix.csv — mapping of egress categories, NAT behavior, and logging emission points (edge gateway, LB, host agent).

Key notes for SIG reviewers:
- Cross-tenant isolation is enforced via tenant-specific compute pools and network-level microsegmentation; data paths are single-tenant by default unless explicit multi-tenant routing is configured for specific workloads.
- Control-plane endpoints are logically and network-segmented from inference hosts; customer-managed VPC endpoints for KMS/HSM are supported in Private mode.
- All egress is denied by default; whitelists require a recorded authorization workflow and are subject to audit logging.

Attachments (redacted): redwood_dedicated_private_isolation_v2.pdf, network_traffic_flows.svg, egress_policy_matrix.csv
